FAIR by Design · Take-home

FAIR Self-Assessment Checklist

Check one research object (a dataset, workflow, software repository or protocol) against the 15 FAIR principles from the workshop. Wherever you answer Partly or No, the fix and the right resource open up.

  • Answer Yes only if you can point to a file or URL as evidence. Note it in the evidence line.
  • Never invent a DOI, license, unit or clinical definition. Write "unknown, requires clarification".
  • Accessible does not mean open. Controlled access can be fully FAIR.

Optional: scan my work first

Drop a folder or files from your own dataset, code repository or protocol. The scan looks for the files a FAIR package normally has (README, metadata, data dictionary, license, provenance, scripts) and suggests an answer for each principle, with the file that is the evidence. You confirm every answer. Anything it cannot judge is left to you, with a short instruction on how to check it.

Drop a folder or files here

Files are read inside your browser. This page has no server and sends nothing anywhere. Do not scan identifiable patient or participant data: use a de-identified sample, or skip the scan and answer the questions yourself. Zip files are not opened (unzip them first). PDF and Word files are recognized by name only.

My first fix

A low score is a starting point. Start with the item that is cheapest to fix, such as a README, a data dictionary, a license statement or recorded software versions.
